key_claims: Dementia risk factors vary widely across countries.
Low education affected 85.6% of older adults in China but only 12.0% in the United States.
High BMI was found in 44.9% of Americans compared with 13.3% of people in India.
Cardiovascular conditions such as high cholesterol and hypertension frequently clustered together, while behaviors like smoking and drinking also tended to occur as groups.
The study analyzed data from more than 214,000 older adults from 14 countries and regions.
limitations: The study used data from 2009 to 2023, which may not reflect current trends.
The study only examined 12 modifiable risk factors identified by the Lancet Commission.
The study did not include all countries, and data collection is ongoing in additional countries.
The study was presented at a conference and published in a journal, but the source does not specify peer review status.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that dementia can be prevented.
The study shows that a single global approach to dementia prevention is ineffective.
The study identifies all possible dementia risk factors.
The study provides causal evidence for the risk factors.

key_claims: A four-month trial involved 315 adults with central obesity.
Completing 75 minutes of brisk interval walking in a single weekly session reduced body fat.
The single weekly session trimmed waistlines.
The single weekly session improved cardiovascular fitness.
The effects were about as effective as splitting the same exercise across three days.
limitations: The source does not specify the exact amount of reduction in body fat or waistline.
The source does not specify the exact improvement in cardiovascular fitness.
The source does not specify the age range or other characteristics of the participants.
The source does not specify the duration of each interval or the intensity of the brisk walking.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that this exercise regimen prevents heart disease or other health conditions.
The study shows that this exercise regimen is superior to other forms of exercise.
The study indicates that this exercise regimen is safe for all adults with central obesity.
The study suggests that this exercise regimen can replace all other physical activity recommendations.

key_claims: Consuming less protein could have greater health benefits than consuming more.
Protein restriction may extend lifespan in some cases.
Protein restriction slows aging by improving metabolism.
Protein restriction changes how cells respond to nutrients.
Protein restriction reduces cellular damage and preserves healthy cell function.
limitations: The source is a review, not a primary study.
The source does not specify the exact amount of protein restriction.
The source does not specify the population (e.g., humans, animals) studied.
The source does not provide evidence for the claims beyond the review's existence.
what_not_to_say: The source does not say that protein restriction definitely extends lifespan in humans.
The source does not say that all protein-fortified foods are harmful.
The source does not provide specific dietary recommendations.
The source does not say that protein restriction is beneficial for everyone.
